pairs.subject: build-economics
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:68 The dev profile only sets `incremental = true`. It has no debug-info dial for dependencies, and nothing in the repo prunes `target/`, which measured 5.3 GB on 2026-10-24 (deps 3.5 GB, incremental 1.6 GB, debug profile only), so the build's disk use grows with no budget and no reaper.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:69 The incremental cache is on but has no byte ceiling and no pruner. `git ls-files | xargs grep` for cargo clean/sweep/prune target found nothing. target/ is 5.3 GB. On the plus side, build.rs:22 adds a `rerun-if-changed` key for the `include_str!` input, which matches the 'key on everything that changes the answer' rule.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:68 There is no `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug` override, so third-party crates (tauri, the bundled SQLite in rusqlite, windows-sys) are built with full debug info that nobody steps through. The technique says dependencies should default to minimal debug info. Release side: vite.config.ts:112 sets sourcemap false.

apps/desktop/scripts/dev-source-loc.mjs:52 The source-stamp inspector is an additive opt-in gate. It is off by default, `@babel/core` is imported lazily only when the gate is on (line 54), and `apply: "serve"` keeps it out of builds.

apps/desktop/src/lib/dev/inspector.tsx:11 The default dev variant is the cheap one. The opt-in variant has a named script (package.json `dev:inspect` and `tauri:inspect`), and the blind spot at the gap is stated in the HUD rather than found by surprise.
apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:9 The crate is not published, so no consumer can inherit obligations from it.

pairs.subject: build-economics
pairs.evidence: scripts/build-sidecar.py:21 The expensive PyInstaller freeze is kept out of the daily loop: the shell falls back to `uv run athena serve`, and the 20 MB toolchain sits in an opt-in extra, so iteration never pays for packaging.

techniques.evidence: scripts/build-sidecar.py:21 The cheap path is the default (an unfrozen daemon) and the frozen sidecar is an opt-in variant. The cost of skipping the freeze is stated: a slower start, not a broken app.

scripts/build-sidecar.py:194 Where the full variant is chosen, the script checks that the gated capability's source is actually installed and refuses to build without it (lines 195-200), instead of shipping a sidecar silently missing the capability.
pyproject.toml:46 numpy, keyring and pyinstaller are declared as optional extras, so a consumer who declines one never resolves it. The default has the fewest obligations.

scripts/build-sidecar.py:268 This is a packaging build, which belongs to the sibling release subject, and no build win is claimed. The printed wall-clock carries no cold or warm label (it omits whether `--clean` was passed), so it would not count as an instrument if a claim ever relied on it.
